content: In human anatomy, the forehead, also referred to as the brow, is the bony region of the head located above the eyes. In modern humans, the forehead is generally vertical in orientation and extends upward until it reaches the hairline, where the contour of the head becomes flatter. The muscles associated with the forehead include the frontalis muscle, which is responsible for moving and contracting the scalp in this region. Historically, the pronunciation of the word forehead rhymed with horrid. However, in recent years, the spelling-based pronunciation has become more prevalent in both Received Pronunciation (RP) and General American English.
